Looking at the demo: each colored box's black interior gets filled with a color determined by the interior size — 2x2 interior (4 cells, even) → 2; 1x1 interior (1 cell, odd) → 7. So fill = 7 if interior cell count is odd, else 2.

Test prediction: 1-box and 5-box (2x2 interiors) → 2; 8-box and 9-box (3x3 interiors, 9 cells) → 7.

```python
from collections import deque

def transform(grid):
    H, W = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    seen = [[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            c = grid[i][j]
            if c == 0 or seen[i][j]:
                continue
            q = deque([(i, j)])
            seen[i][j] = True
            cells = [(i, j)]
            while q:
                y, x = q.popleft()
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny, nx = y+dy, x+dx
                    if 0 <= ny < H and 0 <= nx < W and not seen[ny][nx] and grid[ny][nx] == c:
                        seen[ny][nx] = True
                        q.append((ny, nx))
                        cells.append((ny, nx))
            ys = [p[0] for p in cells]; xs = [p[1] for p in cells]
            y0, y1, x0, x1 = min(ys), max(ys), min(xs), max(xs)
            # verify closed box border
            ok = all(grid[y][x] == c for y in range(y0, y1+1) for x in range(x0, x1+1)
                     if y in (y0, y1) or x in (x0, x1))
            if not ok:
                continue
            interior = [(y, x) for y in range(y0+1, y1) for x in range(x0+1, x1)
                        if grid[y][x] == 0]
            if not interior:
                continue
            fill = 7 if len(interior) % 2 == 1 else 2
            for y, x in interior:
                out[y][x] = fill
    return out
```
